source.title: pLM representations unlock metagenomic space beyond homology
source.authors: Lola Le Breton; David Heurtel-Depeiges; D. C. Millar; L. Zetzsche; Robert M. Vernon; C. Langmead; S. Chandar; Quentin Fournier

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares downstream task performance after 200B versus 2T training tokens, testing scale-related downstream behavior with task metrics rather than held-out language-model loss.
record.gate_note: The paper reports downstream benchmark changes with training-token budget, but does not measure held-out pretraining loss or sweep parameter count or compute. Cited scaling-law claims and values used to motivate the study are not recorded as results. The reported 2T cross-dataset structural comparison does not itself measure a scale response.
record.test_reason: Protein masked LMs are trained for 200B vs 2T tokens, and zero-shot downstream scores (DMS, CASP16 contacts, calibration) are compared. This is a new setting (protein LMs) with a two-point result on whether downstream performance improves with training scale (V6). No loss, fits or parameter/compute sweeps are reported, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude data composition, rather than scale, determines what pLMs learn. Longer training improves all zero-shot tasks except NT calibration for UniRef100 models, which they read as memorization of the curated proteome; metagenomic models gain more from longer training.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies training-token budget and measures downstream protein-model benchmarks; it does not fit or evaluate the original held-out-loss scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed response to longer training varies with training data source and calibration position type.
record.problems: The scale comparison uses downstream tasks rather than held-out pretraining loss; the reported comparison is between 200B and 2T tokens, with no fitted scaling curve or uncertainty stated for these changes. The ablation models are stated to be 120M parameters, so the paper does not test parameter-count scaling.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for the reported CASP16 comparison at scale (MGnify AUC 24.1 versus UniRef100 22.8), because it compares data sources at scale rather than reporting a change across training-token budgets. Other data-mixture and specialized-model results do not test the scale relationship in V6.

untested.parts: Predictability of the improvement: only two token budgets are compared, with no fitted trend and no relation to pretraining loss. No parameter-count or compute scaling.
No compute-optimal allocation. The undertraining hypothesis is motivated by citing Hoffmann but not tested.
No power-law form measured for protein models.

missing.what: Per-task relative score changes from 200B to 2T by dataset; text says metagenomic gains are largest on DMS and CASP16 but gives no numbers

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Scale enters only as a two-point token-budget comparison in protein LMs. The CASP16 cross-dataset comparison at 2T (24.1 vs 22.8) is correctly left out as not a scale change. Cited parameter-scaling claims (refs 6-8) and the Hoffmann citation are motivation, not results.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss scaling, parameter-count sweep, or compute sweep.
No small-run loss fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token trends.
No controlled comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
No test of power-law loss scaling across modalities or the listed training regimes.

Tests downstream task scores across two training-token budgets, not their relation to held-out pretraining loss or a power-law fit; conclusions are limited to the evaluated protein-model tasks and data sources.
Does not fit scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits, or compare fitting choices and curve shapes.

rows.subject: UniRef100-trained models
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream evaluation after training for 200B versus 2T tokens.
rows.value: Strong absolute scores early but gain little from additional training.
rows.locator: Results, “Increasing training steps reveals divergent scaling dynamics”; Figure 2A-B
rows.note: The text gives no numerical aggregate change for this model group.
rows.check: The paper gives no aggregate score. Value is qualitative ('gain little'). Fig 2A caption says all UniRef100 tasks improve except NT calibration, so partial is right. The measure should read per-task zero-shot scores, not an aggregate.

rows.locator: Results, “Increasing training steps reveals divergent scaling dynamics”; Figure 2A-B and caption
rows.note: The result is reported for the BFD-trained model group, without per-task numerical changes here.

rows.subject: UniRef100-trained models

conditions.value: NT (non-target) positions; human residue differs from evolutionary consensus

rows.value: Mean drop of 14.1 points with longer training.
rows.locator: Results, “Increasing training steps reveals divergent scaling dynamics”; Figure 2A-B
rows.note: The authors describe this as progressive memorization of the training proteomes.
rows.check: Correct: NT calibration falls a mean 14.1 points from 200B to 2T. The authors read this as memorization of the training proteome. Model size at 2T is not stated explicitly; 120M is the ablation default 'unless stated otherwise'.

relationships.condition: BFD- and MGnify-trained 120M pLMs, all zero-shot tasks; UniRef100 models at T positions; 200B→2T tokens
relationships.reason: Longer training improves all tasks for metagenomic models (R2, R3) with NT calibration gains of 11.2 and 3.1 (R6, R7). UniRef100 T-position calibration improves (R5).
relationships.display_finding: Longer training improves every tested task for metagenomic models, with NT calibration gains of 11.2 and 3.1 for BFD and MGnify, respectively, while UniRef100 T-position calibration also improves.

relationships.reason: UniRef100 models 'gain little from additional training' despite 10x tokens, so the gain depends on the training data (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Zero-shot performance improved little despite a 10× increase in training tokens.

relationships.condition: UniRef100-trained models, calibration at NT positions
relationships.reason: NT calibration drops a mean 14.1 points with 10x more tokens, i.e. a downstream metric worsens with scale (R4).
relationships.display_finding: Training with 10× more tokens reduced NT calibration by a mean of 14.1 points.
